reading: MARA Holdings, headquartered in Hallandale Beach, Florida and trading on NASDAQ under ticker MARA with SEC CIK 0001507605, is one of the largest publicly traded bitcoin miners in the world, led by chief executive Fred Thiel. The company has an unusual corporate history: it was incorporated in 2010 as Marathon Patent Group, a patent holding and litigation company operating through its Uniloc subsidiary, before pivoting toward cryptocurrency and rebranding as Marathon Digital Holdings on March 1, 2021, then adopting its current name, MARA Holdings, on August 29, 2024. As of August 2025, the company held 50,639 bitcoin, making it the second-largest corporate holder of bitcoin. This registry's Texas facility record for MARA corresponds to the company's bitcoin mining site in Granbury, Texas, which a July 2024 Time magazine investigation documented as a source of community noise complaints from nearby residents. MARA also operates a joint venture facility drawing 37 megawatts from the Hardin Generating Station, a coal-fired power plant in Montana, illustrating the company's strategy of colocating mining operations at power generation sites, a pattern shared with other crypto miners in this registry such as Greenidge Generation and Atlas Power. Some trade press coverage has characterized MARA as quietly building AI infrastructure capacity alongside its core bitcoin mining business, though this registry did not independently verify the scale of any such AI-specific buildout.
